about: Reference firing-rate ranges (spikes/s, spontaneous, awake unless noted) used to judge the column's populations. Human data exist only for layer 2/3 (microelectrode arrays sit in L2/3); deep-layer ranges are rodent and approximate, and should be replaced the moment human laminar recordings appear. Ranges are deliberately generous (log-normal rate distributions span an order of magnitude); a population outside its range is a modelling problem, inside it is only 'not ruled out'. Compiled 4 Nov 2026; see scripts/check_rates.py.

L23E.note: putative pyramidal cells, middle temporal gyrus L2/3: ~0.3 Hz mean in sleep (Peyrache 2012); 1.9-2.6 Hz mean across wake/sleep in the same lab's later arrays (as summarised in Cells 11:106, 2022)

L23F.note: putative interneurons (mostly fast-spiking) MTG L2/3: ~2 Hz in sleep (Peyrache 2012), 6.4-8.1 Hz across states (same summary); FS ~5x RS (Peyrache 2012)

L23N.note: SST-like interneurons L2/3: 0.23 Hz (mostly anaesthetised, Nat Commun 2018, PMC5906477), 1.3 Hz (A1, neuroelectro), ~2.4 Hz in active networks 'similar to awake' (PMC4393017)

L4E.note: approximate; L4 regular-spiking cells sparse in awake rodent sensory cortex (Sakata & Harris 2012; Senzai 2019)

L4F.note: PV cells 7.9-9.3 Hz in L2/3 (PMC5906477; neuroelectro); L4 similar or higher

L4N.note: SST-like interneurons; L4 SST cells are more active than L2/3 SST during whisking (Munoz 2017) but still single digits

L5E.note: L5 pyramidal cells are the most active excitatory layer in awake rodent cortex (Sakata & Harris 2009; Senzai 2019)

L5N.note: SST-like interneurons, deep layers (SST firing higher in deep than superficial layers)

sources: Peyrache A et al. (2012) Spatiotemporal dynamics of neocortical excitation and inhibition during human sleep. PNAS 109:1731-1736. Human MTG L2/3, Utah array; RS ~0.3 Hz, FS ~2 Hz (sleep), FS/RS rate ratio ~5, log-normal.
Dehghani N et al. (2016) Dynamic balance of excitation and inhibition in human and monkey neocortex. Sci Rep 6:23176. Same recordings, wake/SWS/REM; RS/FS count ratio 4:1; no rates tabulated.
Le Van Quyen M et al. (2016) High-frequency oscillations in human and monkey neocortex during the wake-sleep cycle. PNAS 113:9363. Same lab/arrays.
Cells 11:106 (2022) review, section on human in-vivo single units: quotes 1.9-2.6 Hz (pyramidal) and 6.4-8.1 Hz (interneurons) for MTG L2/3 across states, citing a 2016 Cash-lab study.
Ison MJ et al. (2011) Selectivity of pyramidal cells and interneurons in the human medial temporal lobe. J Neurophysiol. MTL (not neocortex): pyramidal 0.6 +/- 0.9 Hz, interneurons 6.4 +/- 4.7 Hz.
Nat Commun 2018 (PMC5906477), mouse S1 L2/3: PYR 0.07 Hz, SST 0.23 Hz, PV 7.9 Hz (mostly urethane).
PMC4393017, mouse barrel cortex active slices: SST 2.4 Hz 'similar to awake'.
Sakata S & Harris KD (2009) Neuron 64:404; (2012) Front Neural Circuits 6:109. Rat auditory cortex laminar rates: L2/3 RS sparse, L5 RS most active, FS higher.
Senzai Y, Fernandez-Ruiz A, Buzsaki G (2019) Neuron 101:500. Mouse V1 laminar rates by state.
